summary.text: Samuel Kane, a Republican personal injury attorney from Las Cruces who has run his own practice since 2004, lost the November 3, 2026 election for Attorney General of New Mexico to Raul Torrez.

His campaign listed limits on license-plate-reader surveillance, combating methamphetamine and fentanyl crime, opposing unchecked data-center development and investigating utility rate hikes as priorities.

paragraphs.text: Kane was not born in New Mexico; he moved to Las Cruces from Arizona and has lived there for more than 20 years.
After clerking for Senior U.S. District Judge Robert C. Brack, he opened his own law practice in 2004, focusing largely on personal injury cases.
His campaign site describes him as an attorney with decades of experience "fighting for the rights of New Mexicans."
Kane advanced from the June 2, 2026 Republican primary for Attorney General with 96,092 votes as the only candidate on the ballot.
He describes his platform as constitutional conservative, with community safety first.
Kane is an avid cyclist, a pilot and a father, and his wife, Jessica, is his partner in business.
He received 37.0% of the vote to Raul Torrez's 63.0%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
